profile.database: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit
profile.note: Controlled historical measurement cutoffs cross a UTC hour; wall-clock engine scheduling is outside this query experiment. Single-query diagnostic control; no independent raw oracle or equivalence claim. Eligibility covers all backfill before initial seeding; initially missing older coverage differs from legacy fixtures.

caveats: Baseline-only diagnostic: candidate and raw oracle are absent; no independent equality claim.
Corrected eligibility changes initial missing coverage; legacy fixture timing is not an unchanged baseline.
Historical backfill still uses direct SQL with fixture provenance, bypassing historical agent grants/buffer/admission; live collection and ingestion are real.
Controlled historical cutoffs cross an hour, not actual wall-clock engine rollover.
Browser renderer shares the server VM; remote capable-client acceptance remains outstanding.
limitations: Sampled occupancy is not a query duration distribution.
No wait event includes runnable CPU and scheduler delay, not necessarily CPU execution.
Cumulative database counters can lag; Docker CPU windows can straddle phase boundaries.
Block I/O and CPU percentages do not prove I/O latency or throttling.
PostgreSQL track_io_timing is off; no per-query I/O duration is established.
Fresh fixture IDs, dispatch and clock/day alignment, baseline latency and publication progress differ. Do not attribute every cross-run timing change solely to retry pacing.
Backfill is a fixed batch count with a minimum pause, not a fixed offered write rate. Faster completion increases competing write throughput during the measured phase.
HTTP spans measure server work; API/browser timings include client scheduling and transport on the same two-vCPU VM.
Trace cohorts use request starts, while ingestion acceptance histograms use completions.

Four failed-labelled extrema trace roots have SQLSTATE 40001. Existing derivedTemporary classification defers serialization conflicts without incrementing durable failure attempts; these spans do not establish terminal failures.
The same observer covers both phases and the preceding control.
This diagnostic does not establish the 1,000-SLO five-minute closed-hour target or actual wall-clock alert-engine rollover.
